In #41944 the author is trying to generalize measurableSet_graph to any codomain with a CountablySeparated measurable space structure. I suggested to the author that we should add the instance that CountablySeparated implies MeasurableEq, but this creates the following two routes of deriving MeasurableEq:

The first route:
MeasurableSingletonClass α + Countable α
-MeasurableSpace.separatesPoints_of_measurableSingletonClass & MeasurableSpace.instCountablyGeneratedOfCountable→ SeparatesPoints α + CountablyGenerated α
-MeasurableSpace.countablySeparated_of_separatesPoints→ CountablySeparated α
-[added in this new PR]→ MeasurableEq α

The second route:
MeasurableSingletonClass α + Countable α
-instMeasurableEqOfMeasurableSingletonClassOfCountable→ MeasurableEq α

Moreover, they are also contained in a cycle as MeasurableEq α → MeasurableSingletonClass α through instMeasurableSingletonClassOfMeasurableEq. How should we fix this problem?

P.S. I have seen posts on Zulip about instance diamonds in the past but this is the first time I encounter such a problem. I am not able to figure out a solution (or a standard way of dealing with this type of problem, although maybe it doesn't exist?) through reading the other similar posts.
is this a problem? docs#MeasurableEq is a Prop-valued class

At least adding the instance does not pass the CI and creates a problem in Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.Dirac and Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Group.Arithmetic, although I think the problem in the first file can be fixed by replacing simp with other tactics (sorry for my ignorance, why being a Prop-valued class potentially makes this not a problem?)

Usually when talking about typeclass diamonds what's happening is that the same typeclass can be synthesized in two different ways, and two results are not defeq at implicit transparency, which will cause problems when unifying the instances. But if it's a Prop-valued class then by proof irrelevance the two values will always be defeq.

After some explorations I think the root cause is that this new instance CountablySeparated β → MeasurableEq β combines with the pre-existing instMeasurableSingletonClassOfMeasurableEq to route every failing MeasurableSingletonClass search into the CountablySeparated instance graph — which does not terminate:

CountablySeparated α
-[countablySeparated_of_hasCountableSeparatingOn]→ HasCountableSeparatingOn α MeasurableSet univ
-[hasCountableSeparatingOn_of_countablySeparated_subtype]→ CountablySeparated ↥(univ : Set α)
-… an infinite tower of subtypes

And I just notice that there's a TODO in the docstring of MeasurableSpace.measurableSingletonClass_of_countablySeparated saying that this theorem should be turned into an instance, and I guess the reason that it was not turned into an instance is the same problem of non-terminating typeclass synthesis.

So maybe something similar should be done to #41944? Make CountablySeparated β → MeasurableEq β a theorem instead of an instance.
I also hit a problem with CountablySeparated in #39739 (see my last message there). I did not take the time to investigate further.

docs#HasCountableSeparatingOn seems like a very weird typeclass to me (why is it On?), it seems to me it should definitely not take the set t as an argument, compare with e.g. docs#CompactSpace and docs#IsCompact
